lines.text: The smoke harness boots the demo Deck App (`js/examples/demo`), presses R through every section, then presses its "Throw an error" Button, comparing a screenshot of each page against `tests/fixtures/golden/Linux/`. `tests/fixtures/demo_stubs.js` is prepended to the demo bundle to pin `Date`, `getTime()` and `fetch`, so the Timers and fetch pages are stable.

The smoke harness boots the demo Deck App (`js/examples/demo`), presses R through every section, then presses its "Throw an error" Button and opens the VitaDeck Shell over the Failure Screen, comparing a screenshot of each against `tests/fixtures/golden/Linux/`. `tests/fixtures/demo_stubs.js` is prepended to the demo bundle to pin `Date`, `getTime()` and `fetch`, so the Timers and fetch pages are stable.

The Deck App input harness (`tests/deck_app_input_harness.c`) runs alongside it: it presses every Pad Button on every section of each example Deck App, then switches to the next, and fails naming the Deck App and button when a Deck App fails or its JS thread hangs. Both carry the `smoke` CTest label, which the macOS `ctest` step excludes.
# A non-ASCII link name, so the Shell golden shows Latin-1, punctuation and CJK fallback glyphs.
# Relative, so the stack trace on the Failure Screen golden does not depend on the build directory.
// The Shell over the canvas, as the main loop draws it.
static bool wait_for_text(const VdBootstrap *bootstrap, const char *text)
// The LAN Listener stays off, so no LAN address reaches the golden.
